front: Give the thesis in one sentence.
back: A computational method that chooses which species replace Porta's plane trees and where, scoring each layout on pedestrian heat stress (UTCI) and event runoff volume, and showing the trade-off (Pareto front).

front: Why will Barcelona replace many plane trees?
back: The tree master plan caps any species at 15%, and plane trees are ~29% of street trees.

front: How much did Barcelona's sealed surface grow, and when?
back: From 45% to 72% of the municipality, 1956–2009.

front: How often do intense storms hit Barcelona?
back: About 3 storms a year exceed 60 mm/h in their first 20 minutes (Barcelona Resilience Atlas).

front: What heat-health fact frames Barcelona's heat problem?
back: It carries one of Europe's highest urban-heat-island mortality burdens (Iungman et al. 2023).

front: Name the six replacement species the city names.
back: Celtis australis, Melia azedarach, Pyrus calleryana, Jacaranda mimosifolia, Tipuana tipu, Brachychiton populneus.

front: Which replacement species has a measured canopy-storage value?
back: Only Pyrus calleryana (Xiao & McPherson 2016). None of the six has a measured cooling value.

front: Which flood type does the thesis address, and which does it exclude?
back: Urban pluvial flooding from frequent, short storms. It excludes river (fluvial) floods and multi-day events on saturated soil.

front: Why was Bologna dropped as a flood case?
back: Its recent floods (Oct 2024, May 2023 Emilia-Romagna) were multi-day, saturated-soil or culvert events where trees have negligible influence.

front: Who is the primary user of the tool?
back: A computational designer working on the municipal street-tree replacement.

front: What is the risk the problem statement points to?
back: Replacement choices can trade away cooling or rain interception without anyone noticing, because most replacement species have no measured storage or cooling value.

front: Where is the study site and how big is it?
back: Porta, Nou Barris, Barcelona; 0.84 km².

front: How many plane trees in Porta, and where are most?
back: 832 plane trees (29% of 2,825 street trees); 194 on Av. Meridiana.

front: What were the two steps of site selection?
back: 1) Eligibility: flood share, surface-heat anomaly and plane density all above the city's 60th percentile. 2) Ranking by the equal-weight mean of four normalised criteria.

front: What does 'non-compensatory' mean in the site selection?
back: A strong value on one hazard cannot make up for the absence of the other: every criterion must pass the threshold first.

front: How was the site choice tested for robustness?
back: Thresholds at the 50th, 60th and 70th percentiles: Porta is first at every threshold. 2,000 random (Dirichlet) weightings: Porta is in the top 3 in 53% of them.

front: Porta's ranks for flood, surface heat and heat vulnerability?
back: Flood #13, surface heat #11 (+1.36 °C), heat vulnerability #12 (91% of area in the top class).

front: What are the four site-selection criteria?
back: Pluvial flood hazard share, summer surface-temperature anomaly (Landsat), social heat vulnerability, plane-tree density.

front: Why is Sant Antoni not the main site?
back: It is #1 for flood but #38 for surface heat (below the city median), so it fails the both-hazards condition. It is the flood-dominant contrast site.

front: What is Florence's role?
back: Transfer test case: run the same method to see if trade-off pattern and species ranking hold.

front: Why does it help that the replacement palette already grows in Porta?
back: Real crowns, heights and LAI of each species can be measured on site from LiDAR.

front: Describe the runoff chain in the model.
back: Rain → canopy interception (storage bucket) over crowns on sealed ground → remaining rain → SCS curve number → event runoff volume.

front: Write the interception equation.
back: I = min(P, S), with S = s · LAI (P rain depth, S canopy storage in mm, s storage per unit LAI).

front: What is the calibrated value of s and its source?
back: s = 1.75 mm per unit LAI, calibrated on Anys & Weiler (2024) Freiburg field data: 16 urban lime and maple trees, 51 storms.

front: What is the lower bound of s in sensitivity runs, and why?
back: 0.86 mm: surface storage only, without evaporation during events (Xiao & McPherson 2016).

front: How much rain does a leafy crown hold at the start of a storm?
back: The first 2–4 mm (Kuehler et al. 2017).

front: Curve numbers used for sealed and pervious surfaces?
back: 98 for sealed surfaces and roofs; 74 for pervious (assumption: TR-55 open space, soil group C).

front: Design storm depths (60 min) for T = 1, 2, 10 years?
back: 19.6 mm, 31.9 mm, 62.5 mm (PDISBA city IDF).

front: Why is the metric runoff volume, not peak flow?
back: In a paired-catchment field study, street trees cut runoff volume ~4% with no peak-flow effect (Selbig et al. 2021).

front: What is the field benchmark for street-tree runoff reduction?
back: 3.5–4% of runoff volume (Coville et al. 2022; Selbig et al. 2021).

front: Why does the tree effect shrink as storms grow?
back: Canopy storage fills in the first few mm; the rest of a big storm passes through, so the intercepted share falls.

front: What is the main trait driving interception?
back: Leaf area index (LAI) / leaf area density; storage capacity also varies threefold among 20 species (Xiao & McPherson 2016).

front: Why are roots not in the scoring?
back: Only two lab studies (Bartens 2008; Zhang 2019): roots raise infiltration, but species differences are unclear (oak vs maple not significant).

front: Why is stemflow ignored?
back: It is < 1% of rain (Anys & Weiler 2024).

front: What is a return period T?
back: The average interval between storms of that size; T = 10 yr means about a 10% chance per year.

front: What sewer design level does Barcelona use?
back: A 10-year return period.

front: What is UTCI?
back: Universal Thermal Climate Index: the 'felt' temperature for a pedestrian, from air temperature, humidity, wind and mean radiant temperature.

front: Which UTCI input do trees change most?
back: Mean radiant temperature (MRT), through shade.

front: UTCI threshold for strong heat stress?
back: UTCI > 32 °C.

front: Write the canopy transmissivity formula.
back: τ = exp(−k · LAI), with k = 0.5 (Beer–Lambert).

front: What is Ladybug Tier 1?
back: Fast point-based UTCI at 1.1 m on a 2 m sidewalk grid, used for many layouts.

front: Two reasons Ladybug underestimates tree cooling.
back: Crowns are opaque without the τ correction (shade MRT off), and it has no evapotranspiration (~2–3 °C UTCI, Mannucci 2025).

front: What is Tier 2 in the heat module?
back: Honeybee UTCI comfort map (Radiance + EnergyPlus) with leaf-on/off transmittance, for a few final layouts.

front: What is Infrared City's role?
back: An AI surrogate API for UTCI in seconds (tutor co-founded it); would replace Tier 1 inside the optimiser. Access still to confirm.

front: Why does the optimiser need a heat proxy?
back: Ladybug costs minutes per layout (20–25 min for 42 trees, Shaamala 2025); 832 positions × many layouts is too slow.

front: Which is the stronger air-cooling term, shade or transpiration?
back: Transpiration (Park 2026: 1.15 °C vs shade 0.43 °C), but it needs soil water.

front: What happened to Platanus in an extreme heatwave?
back: It lost roughly 30–50% of its plant area index after > 41 °C (Sanusi & Livesley 2020) → low-LAI plane variant in sensitivity.

front: Which traits help both heat and runoff?
back: LAI and crown size.

front: Which traits create the heat–runoff conflict?
back: Leaf habit (evergreen vs deciduous) and transpiration / water demand.

front: Why did the leaf-on calendar not create a trade-off?
back: 78% of intense storm days fall in May–Oct (Esbrí et al. 2026), when all palette species are in full leaf.

front: What created the first real trade-off in tool v0?
back: Winter sun access: winter shade on sunlit open ground counted as a cost.

front: Mnemonic for the trade-off finding?
back: Big crowns win both; leaves in winter split them.

front: What is the gap in one sentence?
back: No method selects species and positions using measured traits for both heat and runoff.

front: What is SylvCiT and what is missing?
back: A trait-based AI tree recommender (Nicol et al. 2026, Montreal); its runoff module is disabled, it has no heat, and it uses diversity traits.

front: What does Mannucci et al. 2025 do, and lack?
back: Grasshopper + Ladybug + Kangaroo assess UTCI and runoff, but for fixed scenarios, with no species traits and no optimisation.

front: Which works optimise trees for heat only?
back: Shaamala et al. 2025 and Peng et al. 2026 (Shaamala names water sensitivity as future work).

front: What is the closest precedent?
back: Tan & Liu 2026: NSGA-II + Random Forest surrogate in Grasshopper, species and positions of 30 trees for UTCI, CO2 and diversity.

front: What does this thesis add to Tan & Liu 2026?
back: Runoff, the city's own replacement palette, and the seasons (leaf calendar, winter sun). They used 4 Chicago species, US allometry, one summer hour.

front: Why is the trait data gap itself a finding?
back: Most of the city's replacement species have no measured storage or cooling value; the method has to fill gaps with ranges, and the gap is reported.

front: State the research question (short form).
back: In Porta, which replacement species and positions jointly reduce UTCI (peak summer hour) and event runoff volume (1-, 2-, 10-yr storms), and how large is the trade-off vs current trees, like-for-like and single-objective layouts?

front: What is H1?
back: Synergy: with the same number and size class of trees, trait-based layouts beat like-for-like replacement on both UTCI and runoff, because crown size and LAI drive both.

front: What is H2?
back: Trade-off: heat-optimal and runoff-optimal layouts differ mainly in species (leaf habit, transpiration), not positions; the Pareto front is not a single point.

front: What is H3?
back: Validity boundary: the runoff benefit shrinks as the return period grows; extreme events (6 Sept 2018, ≈300-yr) are outside what trees can affect.

front: Mnemonic for the three hypotheses?
back: S-T-B: Synergy, Trade-off, Boundary.

front: Which comparison tests each hypothesis?
back: H1: S4 vs S1 on both objectives. H2: species of S2 vs S3. H3: runoff benefit vs return period.

front: List scenarios S0–S4.
back: S0 current trees; S1 like-for-like palette; S2 heat-only optimum; S3 runoff-only optimum; S4 multi-objective Pareto set.

front: Mnemonic for S0–S4?
back: Now, Swap, Hot, Wet, Both.

front: Which optimiser is planned, and what does v0 use?
back: NSGA-II (pymoo or Wallacei); v0 uses a weighted-sum linear program (HiGHS).

front: Optimisation constraints?
back: ≤ 15% per species; Shannon diversity floor; no invasive or pest-host species; crown clearance from façades.

front: Which LiDAR, and why is its date useful?
back: ICGC LiDAR flown 26 Sept 2021, leaf-on, ≥ 8 pts/m², CC BY 4.0: gives tree height, crown, LAI proxy, buildings and DTM.

front: What does topo.py do?
back: Priority-Flood flow routing on the DTM + buildings: water convergence and flow distance to flood hotspots.

front: What does heat.py compute?
back: Sun position, building shadows, elliptical shadows of ellipsoid crowns with opacity from LAI and leaf month; summer shade = benefit, winter shade = cost.

front: What does season.py add?
back: A leaf-on calendar per species and storm months, so runoff is an expected value over the storm season.

front: Rule for every parameter in tool code?
back: It is either sourced (cited) or marked ASSUMPTION.

front: Name three ASSUMPTION parameters in the tool.
back: CAPTURE_M = 100 m (flow path to hotspot), OP_BARE = 0.35 (leafless crown opacity), R_OFF = 0.5 (leaf-off LAI ratio).

front: What are the two front-ends of the tool?
back: Grasshopper (primary, computational designer, with Ladybug) and a later web app for non-technical users using the fast heat proxy.

front: How are species without measurements handled?
back: Genus or leaf-habit class values with a range; every result re-run at the low and high end (sensitivity).

front: How much do Porta's current street trees cut runoff (T2-60)?
back: 1.85% of total runoff (2.9% on open space); range 0.4–4.0% across s and T.

front: What happens to runoff during the transition to young trees?
back: Any young replacement ≈ +0.7% runoff ≈ 37% (more than a third) of the current street-tree benefit lost.

front: What did Cortinovis et al. 2022 find for Barcelona?
back: 20,170 new street trees raised runoff retention only from 50.18% to 50.76% for a 20 mm event (city-wide, trees as land cover).

front: Optimised vs random palette, summer shade (tool v0)?
back: +14% summer shade; robust across 7 sensitivity variants.

front: What is the no-regret swap?
back: Summer-only → balanced layout: ~100 Tipuana swapped for Jacaranda, same summer shade, 9% less winter shade.

front: How does placement follow the buildings?
back: Winter-bare Jacaranda goes to positions sunny in winter; winter-leafed species go where buildings already shade the street.

front: Did any replacement layout reach S0?
back: No: mature planes still give more shade than any replacement layout.

front: Open problem found in tool v0?
back: Hotspot runoff does not follow the runoff weight; the per-position water potential predicts it poorly.

front: Name four limits to state openly.
back: Flood index not depth; LiDAR LAI proxy probably low; same s for all species; volume only (no sewer, routing to outlets or ponding). Also: airport EPW, no night effects.

front: Which TRL and innovation type should you claim?
back: TRL 3 (experimental proof of concept on Porta); process innovation delivered as a tool.

front: What is missing according to the seminar checklist?
back: Stakeholder validation (interviews, user walkthrough), an actor map, and naming innovation type and TRL.

front: Answer: 'Is a 2% effect worth a thesis?'
back: The thesis is the method and the trade-off, not a big runoff number; H3 states the limit openly, and the heat side may dominate.

front: Answer: 'What if the scope is too narrow?'
back: Widen the tree into a system: add the tree pit as one design variable; soil as 2–3 literature options; carbon reported, not optimised.
